text:
Priya: Heads-up — I just finished a dry run bringing up a community 7B model (atlas-7b) from HF to Redwood and hit a few config mismatches that broke chat-style inference. Posting notes in case anyone else sees this.

Noah: What broke exactly? latency? correctness?

Priya: Conversations were truncating midsentence when we hit ~2048 tokens even though HF config had max_position_embeddings: 4096. Looks like our conversion clipped the value to 2048 somewhere.

onboard-bot: Conversion pipeline report: missing_field: sliding_window -> defaulted to true; rope_scaling -> warning: unrecognized format; num_key_value_heads mismatch detected.

Jules: Hmm. We recently added a safety cap for max_position_embeddings in the converter because some HF configs lied. But defaulting to 2048 is too aggressive for chat models. Can you paste the original config snippet?

Priya: Sure — original HF model config (sanitized):
```json
{
  "model_type": "gpt_neox",
  "max_position_embeddings": 4096,
  "num_key_value_heads": 32,
  "rope_scaling": {"type": "linear", "factor": 1.0},
  "sliding_window": false
}
```

Priya: And the converted config that Redwood ended up with (excerpt):
```json
{
  "max_position_embeddings": 2048,
  "num_key_value_heads": 16,
  "rope_scaling": 1.0,
  "sliding_window": true
}
```

Noah: Yikes — the converter both downscoped max_position_embeddings and flipped sliding_window to true. Also changed the shape/semantics of rope_scaling. That would explain both early truncation and some attention mismatch artifacts.

Jules: Definitely a bug. The num_key_value_heads change is especially dangerous: if KV head count is halved but weights are left in a single chunk we get misaligned projections at runtime. Did you see bad logits or just truncation?

Priya: Both. Truncation first, but when I forced 4096 in the runtime it produced subtle attention artifacts (heads pointing at odd offsets) and generated repetitions. Quantized int8 run had worse hallucination rate.

Noah: My hypothesis: converter tried to normalize some models to our internal 16-head layout for performance heuristics, and also coerced rope_scaling into a float (legacy behavior). That will silently break positional math.

Jules: Action items: (1) add a hard assertion in the converter that preserves max_position_embeddings if HF explicitly sets it, unless user overrides; (2) preserve rope_scaling structure (objects vs scalar) and translate fields with explicit mapping; (3) emit a conversion-time warning when num_key_value_heads differs and require explicit opt-in to remap; (4) add unit test that runs a short chat trace and compares attention patterns.

Priya: Agreed. I can open a PR with tests. Quick patch suggestion I used locally: in convert_config.py detect keys like 'rope_scaling' with dict -> map to our rope_scaling dict, else if float raise a warning. Also keep max_position_embeddings as-is unless > 65536 or absurd.

Noah: For num_key_value_heads remapping, we can implement a safe projection step: if HF_n_kv_heads % rw_kv_heads == 0, we allow tiled mapping and add a deterministic identity mapping table; otherwise fail with an error asking user to rerun converter with --force-head-remap.

Jules: Good idea. Also add a small script that compares the converted config to the HF source and prints a human diff (fields changed, types changed). That would have caught this earlier.

Priya: I'll include that diff output in the PR. Example output I want:
```
- max_position_embeddings: 4096 -> 2048 (type preserved int)
- sliding_window: false -> true (bool changed)
- num_key_value_heads: 32 -> 16 (potential correctness risk)
- rope_scaling: {type: linear, factor: 1.0} -> 1.0 (type changed dict->float)
```

onboard-bot: Ticket created: ONB-4123 "converter: preserve HF config semantics for position/rope/kvheads" (pri=high)

Noah: Nice. One more gotcha we saw previously — tokenizer special tokens and chat templates can also assume different positional offsets when max_position_embeddings changes. Make sure the diff step flags templates that rely on specific offsets.

Priya: Will do. I'll also run our eval harness (LM-evals subset) on the patched converter to check for regression. If anyone wants to repro: I pushed a minimal reproduction branch `priya/hf-config-diff` with a script `scripts/repro-convert.sh`.

Jules: Thanks — leave a note in the PR with the eval logs, especially attention heatmaps before/after. :thumbsup:

Priya: Will do. Posting the PR in ~15m.

Noah: Thanks for catching this early — could have bit a customer during rollout.

Priya: Yup. Follow-up: adding a README entry for model bring-up checklist (tokenizer, config diff, chat template run) so oncall knows to run it before marking a model as ready.

Jules: Love that. End-to-end checklist would have prevented this.
